clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Article 12(1) were violated by his arrest and detention.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed violation of his right to equality under Article 12(1) due to arbitrary arrest and detention, alleging mala fide actions by police because of his political affiliation.
case_context.respondent_argument: No submissions were made to the Court regarding Article 12(1) at the hearing; the respondents did not materially engage with this claim.
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested on 20 July 1984 and detained until 30 August 1984.
Petitioner alleged mala fide detention due to political reasons.
No substantive submissions were made on Article 12(1) during the hearing.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court noted that the material set out in the petition was insufficient to establish a claim under Article 12(1).
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since no submissions were made and the evidence did not support discrimination or inequality claims, the Court found no violation of Article 12(1).
principles_established: Claims under Article 12(1) require sufficient material to establish inequality or discrimination.
Failure to make submissions or provide evidence on a constitutional claim can lead to dismissal of that claim.

outcome.holding: The petitioner's claim under Article 12(1) was dismissed for lack of sufficient material and submissions.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: The petitioner alleged violation of equality rights under Article 12(1), but the Court found no material or submissions to support this claim, leading to dismissal.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner’s claim under Article 12(1) was not supported by submissions or sufficient material, and the Court dismissed this claim accordingly.
